deep.reconstruction:
Context: Physicalisches Cabinet, Göttingen, 17 Dec 1834, a.m. This page continues the previous page's log of scale readings of a magnetometer bar in the physics cabinet. On the previous page Gauss notes the bar's position after 'die Verbindung mit der Sternwarte gelöst war', so the bar was connected by the Gauss–Weber wire circuit to a second magnetometer at the observatory. The next page fits these records with sums of two damped-free harmonic terms.

(1) Reading table, 11h34'0" to 11h37'9". Readings x(t) are taken every 7 s.
- The second column is NOT the mean of adjacent readings. It is the mean of the readings 7 s before and 7 s after the listed instant: y(t) = [x(t-7)+x(t+7)]/2. Example: y(34'7") = (499.0+497.5)/2 = 498.25; y(34'14") = (500.5+495.8)/2 = 498.15. This was verified for every entry (see errors).
- Why this works: the bar's own free swing has swing time (Gauss's Schwingungsdauer, i.e. half period) of about 14 s, so its period is about 28 s. Next page: n = 90°/7 per second. Readings 14 s apart are in opposite phase of that swing, so averaging them cancels it.
- What survives is the slow oscillation with 7N ≈ 30°3' (next page). That is a period of about 7·360/30.05 ≈ 84 s, cf. '+83.6' on the previous page. It is attenuated only by the factor cos 7N = cos 30° ≈ 0.866 [my remark].
- The smoothed column indeed shows this slow wave: maxima ≈502.9 at 34'56" and ≈502.6 at 36'20", i.e. 84 s apart; amplitude ≈2.3; minima ≈498.2 at 35'31" and ≈498.5 at 36'55".
- So the slow motion is that of the coupled observatory magnetometer, transmitted inductively through the circuit. The fast component is the cabinet bar's own swing.

(2) Note: 'für die Schwingung von 14" besser 13"68'. The swing time of the fast oscillation is better taken as 13.68 s instead of the 14 s assumed in the reductions (n = 90°/7 per s).

(3) Phase/amplitude table, headed 'a sin A' over 'c' (header meaning not certain). Each row gives a time (min:sec after 11h), a phase written as (integer, degrees), and a number.
- The integer is evidently a count of full cycles of the fast oscillation. The total phase Φ = 360k + φ grows linearly with time.
- Times relative to 9'12" and total phases:
  - 0 s: 354.25°
  - 70 s: 1273.55°
  - 189 s: 2837.23°
  - 330 s: 4691.7°
  - 428 s: 5988.41°
  - 592 s: 8143.23°
  - 1516 s: 20172.10°
  - 1649 s: 21921.34°
- From the first row to the sixth (the underlined row 19'4"): (8143.23-354.25)/592 = 13.157°/s. Half period = 180/13.157 = 13.681 s, which is exactly the '13"68' of the note [my reconstruction of how the figure was obtained]. The rows 9'12"–19'4" (beginning series) give it.
- The two later rows (34'28", 36'41"; end series) give a mean rate of ≈13.08°/s from the start (≈13.76 s). Between themselves: (21921.34-20172.10)/133 = 13.15°/s, again ≈13.68 s. So the cycle counts are consistent within each group, and the group-to-group link is slightly looser.
- Third column (1.58, 1.70, 2.78, 2.86, 2.75, 2.73, 2.64, 2.68): almost certainly the amplitude c of the fast oscillation in scale divisions. It grows from ≈1.6 at the start to ≈2.7. Compare the next page: beginning 1.46, middle 2.52, end 2.83.

Purpose: separate the two superposed oscillations in the inductively coupled two-magnetometer system. The aim is to determine the swing time, phase and amplitude of the cabinet bar's own oscillation and the 84-s induced oscillation. These feed the harmonic representations written on the next page.
errors: Entry at 11h34'28": the mean (495.8+503.3)/2 = 499.55, but the page reads 499.65 (possibly a slip, or a misreading of an overwritten digit).
Entry at 11h36'48": the correct mean is (498.3+499.4)/2 = 498.85. The machine transcription gives 499.85, but the image shows a corrected digit, apparently 498.85, so Gauss's value is right.
All other smoothed values check exactly.

The 13.68 s swing time is consistent with rows 1–6 of the phase table. Linking to the last two rows over the gap implies ≈13.76 s overall, a mild inconsistency (≈0.5% in rate), possibly due to phase drift or a cycle-count/epoch issue. This is not a clear error.

results.what: Removal of a known periodic component (period 28 s) from equally spaced readings by averaging readings separated by half its period, leaving the slower 84-s oscillation (attenuated by cos 30°)
results.modern_name: Moving-average / comb filtering (notch at a known frequency)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard technique of 19th-century observational practice (Gauss–Weber magnetic method of 'Elongationen' and averaging)

results.what: Determination of the oscillation period from phase progression with integer cycle counting over many minutes (swing time 13.68 s vs assumed 14 s)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard in Gauss–Weber magnetometry (Intensitas, 1832; Resultate des magnetischen Vereins)

results.what: Analysis of two coupled magnetometers linked by a wire circuit (induced currents transmitting the 84-s oscillation of one bar to the other; amplitude growth of the fast swing)
results.modern_name: Electromagnetic induction coupling of oscillators / galvanometer–induction experiments
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber, 1833–1838 (Göttingen telegraph line, induction experiments)

deep.surprise_reason: These are laboratory data reduction notes from the known Gauss–Weber induction/telegraph experiments: smoothing to suppress the bar's free swing, harmonic phase/amplitude tracking, and correction of the swing time. The methods are routine for Gauss and the experiments are documented; only the specific numbers are unpublished detail.

checkable.asserts: Swing time from rows 9'12" to 19'4" of the phase table ≈ 13.681 s, matching '13"68'
Swing time from first to last row ≈ 13.76 s
Period of the slow oscillation from 7N = 30°3'12" ≈ 83.9 s
Averaging readings 7 s apart multiplies a harmonic by cos(7w); this is 0 for w = pi/14 (28-s period) and cos(pi/6) for the 84-s component

transcription_corrections: 11h36'48": second column appears to read 498.85 (digit corrected), not 499.85; it matches the computed mean.
11h34'28": second column printed 499.65, but the computed mean is 499.55; the digit may be ambiguous.
Note line reads 'für die Schwingung von 14" besser 13"68' (Schwingung = swing time).
